derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the genitive case of G3956 (πᾶς);

occurrences.text: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God.
By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
